διδόναι [to give] in expressions conveying the notion of a single verb. Thus δίκην διδόναι [to give justice] means to pay the penalty, i.e., to be punished.
passive

[The forms of the verb in Aeschylus are the same as in all other authors. However, it should be noted that διδοῖ [he gives] (as if from διδόω) is used for δίδωσι [he gives] in Suppl. 1010, which Homer, Pindar, Herodotus, and others sometimes used. Since not all moods of the first and second aorist are in use, the singular indicative is taken from the first aorist, ἔδωκα [I gave], while the plural and the remaining moods are from the second, ἔδομεν [we gave], δός [give], δοίην [may I give], δῶ [I may give], δοῦναι [to give], δούς [having given].] It is construed with the dative of the person, either expressed or understood, and the accusative of the thing, or with an infinitive.
